authority: apostila-cga-2026; adversarial review round 2, gaps R1/R2/R4
method: exhaustive re-sweep of `prêmio` (7 occurrences) and `capital` (23) against their current definitions; the two declared restorations tested against the corpus text they claimed to restore
reason: A narrowing that was not followed by a sweep, a bare form absorbing five distinct senses, and two collocations written from paraphrase instead of from the text.

operations.why: Amendment 3 narrowed this definition to `the amount paid above a reference value` and did not re-sweep the form, which is the exact discipline that amendment applied to entity.distribution in the same file. Against the narrowed definition only `ÁGIO (prêmio): O título está mais caro` fits; the rest are an insurance premium, a CDS premium twice, a risk premium and a liquidity premium. Bare `prêmio` carries four unrelated senses here and none of them has a distinguishing collocation except liquidity, so review is the correct outcome — `ágio` keeps the above-par sense on technical.premium_price.

Defined as `the capital available to be allocated by a manager` and matching `ganhos de capital`, `capital aberto`, `juros sobre capital próprio`, `Estrutura de capital`, `capital subscrito`, `capital econômico`, `capital regulatório` and `Morgan Stanley Capital International`. `recursos` keeps the concept anchored and the absorbed senses are now their own concepts.

`Morgan Stanley Capital International` is the compound-fragment class in a proper name — the same defect as `Hedge Funds`, and invisible to find_compound_fragments.py because it occurs once and the script required two.

operations.form: desconto sobre o valor de face
operations.why: The collocation I registered to restore this sense does not match the corpus, which writes `desconto sobre SEU valor de face`. Written from a paraphrase rather than from the text — the same mistake as the translated Portuguese labels, made while repairing that mistake.
The prefix both occurrences share, verified against the text.

technical.yield_spread owns this exact phrase and technical.yield also claimed it, so the collision demoter sent BOTH to review and the expression the corpus uses for a yield spread matched nothing at all. Withdrawing the wrong claim restores it.
Held at review only by the collision withdrawn above.
`reports/compound-fragments.json` reported `Yield` at fragment_share 1.0 with `Os Yield Spreads` among its compounds and the plural was never registered.
